reviewers.summary: The investigator gates model calls, but its authorization request omits data returned by read tools. A fetched page can therefore reach a later model call without the gate checking that page content.

findingList.message: Include fetched tool results in the data checked by ModelCallGate.Authorize before they reach a subsequent model call; currently the gate authorizes only the initial documents, leaving fetched page content unchecked.

evidence.codePathTraced: GatedModelClient authorizes each call using only the documents captured when InvestigateAsync starts. CaseReadTools can return additional page text, which FunctionInvokingChatClient sends in a later model call, but that text is not included in the authorization request.
evidence.failureScenario: If the case source returns a page containing data absent from the initial documents, the model can fetch it and receive it on a subsequent call while ModelCallGate.Authorize checks only the initial documents. Unapproved data can therefore reach the model without being checked by the gate (LLM02:2025).

reviewers.summary: The tests cover the main investigator behaviors, but do not verify the required limit hook before tool calls. A regression removing those calls would pass the named test suite.

findingList.message: Add a test that invokes a read tool and asserts BeforeToolCallAsync runs. The current limit test covers model calls only, leaving the per-tool limit behavior in the acceptance criteria unprotected.

evidence.codePathTraced: The acceptance criterion requires IInvestigationLimits to be called before each tool and model call. Every_model_call_is_gated_and_recorded_as_a_trace exercises a response that makes no tool calls, and CountingLimits does not count or assert BeforeToolCallAsync.
evidence.failureScenario: If the BeforeToolCallAsync calls are removed from CaseReadTools, this test still passes. The required per-tool limit behavior can regress without the named test detecting it.

reviewers.summary: Most document-derived tool results are delimited, but inventory identifiers are returned raw. If identifiers can contain attacker-controlled text, that creates a prompt-injection path.

findingList.message: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection: delimit or validate inventory identifiers before returning them to the model; attacker-controlled identifiers can carry instructions outside the untrusted-data boundary.

evidence.codePathTraced: The investigator exposes get_case_inventory, which returns source.GetInventory(caseId) values directly to the model without the untrusted-data delimiter used for other case-derived tool results.
evidence.failureScenario: If a case document identifier can contain attacker-controlled text, an identifier containing instructions can reach the model as active text when it calls get_case_inventory, potentially influencing its claims (LLM01:2025).
